items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 4.8.3 at source lines 821-826: for any type B the map chi sending a pair (A,f) and a point b to the fiber of f at b is an equivalence from Sigma A:type, (A -> B) to B -> type. The author's proof (source lines 827-850) is an explicit quasi-inverse construction in which the two round trips require different inputs: the first is immediate from the retained lemma computing the fiber of a projection (lines 836-839), while the second needs a path between two elements of a sigma type, which is reduced by the sigma-path characterisation to the transport equation trans (ua(e)) proj1 = f (lines 840-847) and then discharged by combining the univalence computation rule with the retained transport-arrow identity, the inverse map e^{-1} being defined precisely so that the composite is definitionally f (line 848). The statement is a single equivalence and hides that the second round trip is a transport computation along a univalence path.
